newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: S.African advisers arrive in Kabila's Congo.
newsitem.headline: S.African advisers arrive in Kabila's Congo.

text.p: A South African government team flew into Kinshasa on Tuesday to advise President Laurent Kabila on rebuilding his Congo's monetary system.
Analysts say President Nelson Mandela is keen to nurture influence over the new rulers of former Zaire, Africa's third- largest country and potentially one of its richest.
"This is a first exploratory visit to see if there are areas where we have the knowledge and capability to help," South African ambassador Jan van Deventer told Reuters.
"It's a get-to-know-you visit, there are no deals on the table at the moment."
Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad led a team that includes officials from the central Reserve Bank, the Development Bank of Southern Africa and the finance and trade departments.

Deventer said a Tuesday meeting with Kabila had been postponed but would hopefully be rescheduled before the end of the visit on Tuesday. The group also planned to see officials from the foreign and finance ministries.

South Africa this year launched a late diplomatic effort to broker a peaceful settlement between Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko and advancing rebel leader Kabila, but the talks faltered and Kabila drove Mobutu into exile last month.

Various governments, mining companies and other business interests are now knocking on Kabila's door, hoping the new government will open up the underdeveloped country and revive an economy which imploded under Mobutu's 32-year misrule.
South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki was the first senior African leader to visit Kabila after he declared himself president of the renamed Democratic Republic of Congo in May.
The group from Africa's most industrialised nation did not include expected representatives of its important mining sector.
The foreign ministry in Pretoria said the team's visit answered a response for assistance from Kabila's government.
